title: Open module transposes are linear morphisms and commute with composition
statement:
Let $X$ be a topological space, $\mathcal O_X$ a sheaf of commutative rings, and $U\subseteq X$ open. Put $\mathcal O_U(W)=\mathcal O_X(W)$ for opens $W\subseteq U$, with inherited restrictions. Work with module presheaves (abelian presheaves with sectionwise module actions and semilinear restrictions) and sectionwise linear morphisms [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification]. Suppose $\mathcal P,\mathcal P'$ are $\mathcal O_X$-module presheaves and $\mathcal Q,\mathcal Q'$ are $\mathcal O_U$-module presheaves. On opens of $U$ write $R\mathcal P(W)=\mathcal P(W)$ with inherited actions and restrictions; on opens of $X$ write $D\mathcal Q(V)=\mathcal Q(V\cap U)$ with the restrictions of $\mathcal Q$ and the $\mathcal O_X(V)$-action through ring restriction $\rho_V:\mathcal O_X(V)\to\mathcal O_U(V\cap U)$. Assume these assignments have the indicated module-presheaf structures, and for morphisms put $(R\mu)_W=\mu_W$ and $(D\nu)_V=\nu_{V\cap U}$. For every module-presheaf morphism $\alpha:R\mathcal P\to\mathcal Q$, the components
$$\Phi(\alpha)_V(s)=\alpha_{V\cap U}(s|_{V\cap U})$$
define an $\mathcal O_X$-linear module-presheaf morphism $\mathcal P\to D\mathcal Q$. For every module-presheaf morphism $\beta:\mathcal P\to D\mathcal Q$, the components
$$\Psi(\beta)_W(s)=\beta_W(s)\quad(W\subseteq U)$$
(using $D\mathcal Q(W)=\mathcal Q(W)$ and $\rho_W=\mathrm{id}$) define an $\mathcal O_U$-linear module-presheaf morphism $R\mathcal P\to\mathcal Q$. For every $\mu:\mathcal P'\to\mathcal P$, $\nu:\mathcal Q\to\mathcal Q'$ and $\alpha:R\mathcal P\to\mathcal Q$, these forward maps satisfy
$$\Phi(\nu\circ\alpha\circ R\mu)=D\nu\circ\Phi(\alpha)\circ\mu.$$
Their common component at any open $V\subseteq X$ sends $s\in\mathcal P'(V)$ to $\nu_{V\cap U}(\alpha_{V\cap U}(\mu_{V\cap U}(s|_{V\cap U})))$. These conclusions apply in particular to module sheaves and their morphisms [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category].

proof.text:
Put $A=V\cap U$. By [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification], restriction in $\mathcal P$ is additive and semilinear over $\rho_V$, and $\alpha_A$ is additive and $\mathcal O_X(A)$-linear. Thus $\Phi(\alpha)_V(s+t)=\alpha_A(s|_A)+\alpha_A(t|_A)$. For $a\in\mathcal O_X(V)$,
$$\Phi(\alpha)_V(as)=\alpha_A(\rho_V(a)s|_A)=\rho_V(a)\alpha_A(s|_A)=a\cdot\Phi(\alpha)_V(s),$$
where the last action is precisely the stipulated action on $D\mathcal Q(V)$. This proves sectionwise $\mathcal O_X$-linearity, including preservation of zero.

source.place: Tag 008U (sheaves-lemma-adjoint-push-pull-presheaves-modules), proof, compatibility with module structures; open section model of Tag 00A0 (sheaves-lemma-j-pullback), (1) and final sentence.

proof.text:
For an inclusion of opens $V'\subseteq V$, put $A=V\cap U$ and $B=V'\cap U$. Naturality of $\alpha$ and composition of restrictions give
$$\bigl(\Phi(\alpha)_V(s)\bigr)|_B=(\alpha_A(s|_A))|_B=\alpha_B((s|_A)|_B)=\alpha_B((s|_{V'})|_B)=\Phi(\alpha)_{V'}(s|_{V'}).$$
The leftmost restriction is exactly that of $D\mathcal Q$. Together with step 1 this is the definition of a module-presheaf morphism [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification].

source.place: Tag 008U (sheaves-lemma-adjoint-push-pull-presheaves-modules), proof, compatibility with module structures; open section model of Tag 00A0 (sheaves-lemma-j-pullback), (1) and final sentence.

proof.text:
For $W\subseteq U$, the identity $W\cap U=W$ identifies the action on $D\mathcal Q(W)$ with the action on $\mathcal Q(W)$, since $\rho_W=\mathrm{id}$. Hence the additive, $\mathcal O_X(W)$-linear map $\beta_W$ is an $\mathcal O_U(W)$-linear map $(R\mathcal P)(W)\to\mathcal Q(W)$. For $W'\subseteq W\subseteq U$, naturality of $\beta$ reads
$$\beta_W(s)|_{W'}=\beta_{W'}(s|_{W'}).$$
Both restrictions here are the inherited ones of $\mathcal Q$ and $R\mathcal P$. Thus these components define $\Psi(\beta)$ as a module-presheaf morphism [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification].

proof.text: For module sheaves the notion of morphism in [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] is exactly an additive restriction-compatible sectionwise linear map, as used above. Restriction preserves the sheaf property: a cover of an open $W\subseteq U$ is the same cover by opens of $X$, so gluing is gluing in $\mathcal P$. Direct image preserves it as well: for a cover $V=\bigcup_iV_i$, the opens $V_i\cap U$ cover $V\cap U$, and compatible sections of $D\mathcal Q(V_i)=\mathcal Q(V_i\cap U)$ glue uniquely in $\mathcal Q(V\cap U)=D\mathcal Q(V)$. Therefore the same maps and equality are morphisms and equality of module sheaves whenever the inputs are sheaves.
